notes:
Auto-updater root cause + four user-feedback polish items. The "Check now" button now actually drives Rust + reports back honestly; the History redesign is rebuilt around two strong shared visuals; calendar empty state diagnoses itself; manual MT5 credentials live behind a disclosure now that auto-detect is the default UX.

### Auto-updater root cause — surface version + Rust verdict to dashboard (P1)

The button has been showing misleading messaging since v1.0.20: "you're on v1.0.27" / "nothing actually installs" was a compounding result of three connected bugs, not a single broken handler.

Root cause chain:

1. `/api/status` never returned a `version` field. Both `bridgeRefreshUpdateStatus` and `loadBridge` read `s.version`, both got undefined, both silently fell to wrong fallbacks. Bridge tab wording fell to "Latest version: vX" — implying an upgrade was available even when the user was current.
2. `bridgeCheckUpdates` compared `bridge-version.textContent` (always empty because of #1) to latest.json. `cur === ''` → `isCurrent` was always false → JS unconditionally offered to install, regardless of actual version match. Rust's marker-file trigger fired correctly, Rust ran `updater.check()`, Tauri compared baked v1.0.27 to latest.json v1.0.27, returned `Ok(None)`, exited silently. User saw only the JS toast "Update triggered" and never a UAC prompt.
3. No disk logging anywhere on the Rust side. `eprintln!` in a release build goes to nowhere on Windows. Zero way for a test user to debug what the updater is actually doing.

Fix:

- Rust passes `TRADESPACE_VERSION = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` at sidecar spawn.
- `run_update_check` writes every state transition to `%APPDATA%/TradeSpace/updater.log` (newline-JSON, self-trims at 256KB).
- `run_update_check` writes the latest result to `%APPDATA%/TradeSpace/last-update-check.json` after each run.
- New `/api/update/last-check` (auth-gated): reads + returns the Rust result file.
- New `/api/update/log` (auth-gated): tails the last 100 lines of `updater.log` for support copy-paste.
- `bridgeCheckUpdates` rewritten — ALWAYS triggers Rust (no JS-side version compare), then polls `/api/update/last-check` at 1.5s for up to 12 attempts, then shows the Rust verdict verbatim (no-update / downloading / installing / error).

This fix won't help users stuck on v1.0.20–v1.0.27 because their running binary still has the old code. They have to install v1.0.28 once manually, after which the Check now button + auto-updater both work.

### Signal-source banner false positive (P2)

The "Signal copier not configured — set up Telegram in Settings" banner was firing for users who had ALREADY connected a signal source. Two compounding gaps:

- v1.0.25 multi-select Telegram users (`telegram_group_ids` populated, legacy `group_id` empty) were treated as unconfigured.
- Discord-only users (channels selected via Bridge tab, Telegram untouched) were told to set up Telegram.

Banner now hides when EITHER source is configured, with wording "No signal source connected — set up Telegram or Discord in Settings."

### Provider Performance v2 — diverging P&L bar + win-rate pill (P3)

User feedback on the v1.0.27 redesign: "not the nicest, all the bars look a bit odd." Three independent inline visualizations per row (a 56px volume microbar, plain colored P&L text, a 3px win-rate fill bar) didn't share a visual language and read as decoration rather than information.

v2 design — ONE strong primary visual + ONE strong secondary, both reused across the Provider table AND the Session strip so the two cards now read as one continuous attribution view.

- **Diverging P&L bar (primary):** centered on a vertical zero line; negative pnl extends LEFT in red, positive extends RIGHT in green. Magnitude proportional to global max-abs across all rows + total — a 50%-wide bar literally means "half the size of the largest contributor." Gradient fills + soft glow. Value text right-justified at the cell's outer edge.
- **Win-rate pill (secondary):** 26px rounded rectangle with a coloured fill BEHIND the percentage text, fill width = win-rate %. Severity-toned border + text (green ≥55, amber ≥45, red <45). Renders the same in provider rows AND session cells.
- Dropped the 56px volume microbar (clutter — trade count number alone tells the story).
- Total row gets bumped weights so the eye lands there after scanning detail rows.

### Economic calendar — diagnose 'no news today' confusion (P4)

User saw "no events" / "no news today" and asked whether the integration was broken. Investigation showed the fetch IS healthy (engine logs: 132 events / 11 high-impact via TradingView every 2 min). The empty list is almost always a filter combination producing zero matches — particularly the default 'Today + USD only' on weekends.

- Smart empty state: when today has zero matches but tomorrow has N, show a quick-switch button "Try Tomorrow (N)". Same fallback for "This Week". Genuine fetch failure points at `%APPDATA%\TradeSpace\logs\debug.log`.
- New `/api/calendar/diagnostics` endpoint returning last-fetch metadata: `{ts, source, events_count, high_impact_count, error, next_retry_secs}` + `cache_size`.
- New feed-freshness chip in the Calendar header. Polls diagnostics every 60s while the tab is open. Green: "Feed: 132 events · TV 47s ago". Amber: fetched-with-errors (fallback used). Red: error and cache empty. The chip's `title` carries the exact error string for support.
- `engine.fetch_economic_calendar` records every fetch into a new `_last_calendar_fetch` dict.

### Hide MT5 manual credentials behind disclosure (P5)

Despite v1.0.22's auto-detect, the manual account/password/server form was always visible on the Profile page — first-time users were typing in their broker password when they didn't need to.

Wrapped in a native `<details>`/`<summary>` disclosure. Closed by default. Summary reads "ADVANCED · MANUAL MT5 CREDENTIALS · Optional" with a hint "Auto-detect already covers most setups. Open only if you need to type a stored credential." Inner copy adds "You usually don't need this." Rotating chevron via CSS `[open]` selector — no JS handler.

### What did NOT land in v1.0.28

- 17 `mt5.order_send` real-money migrations (deferred again — the auto-updater needed proving working first; once users on v1.0.28 are confirmed receiving updates, v1.0.29 can pick up the broker-migration scope).
- ~28 remaining read-side `mt5.*` call sites (`orders_get`, `history_deals_get`, etc.).

### Tests

339/339 python tests pass at every commit boundary. cargo + npm clean.
